**Visual observations from test image:**
- Young soybean seedlings (V1-V2 stage) that are completely dead
- Leaves are thoroughly dried, brown, papery, and curled — still attached to stems
- Stems appear dark/discolored near the base
- Dry appearance (not water-soaked or soft-rotted)
- Healthy plants visible in background — sparse/scattered death pattern

**Candidate narrowing:**
- **Pythium**: Water-soaked soft rot — eliminated by the dry, crispy appearance
- **Phytophthora**: Chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward, wilted leaves staying attached — possible
- **Rhizoctonia**: Dry, firm reddish-brown sunken cankers at soil line, dead/wilted seedlings — matches the dry, desiccated appearance well

**Reference comparison:** The Rhizoctonia reference shows reddish-brown stem lesions at soil line causing complete seedling death — the dry, girdled canker pattern explains the thoroughly desiccated dead seedlings with intact stem structure seen in the test image. The non-water-soaked, firm dry lesion appearance is the key differentiator from Pythium/Phytophthora.
